summary_zh: 學會開會前幾分鐘輕鬆閒聊的說法，並用 although、despite、whereas、however 表達「雖然／儘管／相對地／不過」。

vocab.definition: to say or do something that helps people relax when they first meet or start talking
vocab.example: A quick question about the weekend is an easy way to break the ice.
vocab.example_zh: 問一下週末過得如何，是打破冷場的簡單方法。

vocab.definition: to start to feel comfortable in a new home, job or place
vocab.example: It took me about a month to settle in at the new office.
vocab.example_zh: 我花了大約一個月才適應新辦公室。

vocab.definition: full of activity, with no time to rest
vocab.example: Despite a hectic morning, she joined the call on time.
vocab.example_zh: 儘管早上忙得團團轉，她還是準時上線開會。

vocab.definition: the trip you make between home and work every day
vocab.example: Although my new commute is longer, I can read on the train.
vocab.example_zh: 雖然我新的通勤路程比較長，但我可以在火車上看書。

vocab.definition: to learn all the latest information you need to do a job
vocab.example: Could you help Jun get up to speed before Monday?
vocab.example_zh: 你可以在星期一前幫 Jun 掌握最新狀況嗎？

vocab.example: Sorry, I'm running behind, so please start without me.
vocab.example_zh: 抱歉，我晚了一點，請先開始不用等我。

vocab.definition: getting better after an illness or injury
vocab.example: I had a bad cold last week, but I'm on the mend now.
vocab.example_zh: 我上週重感冒，不過現在慢慢好起來了。

vocab.definition: a request to be told about any news or changes
vocab.example: Good luck with the landlord, and keep me posted on what he says.
vocab.example_zh: 祝你跟房東交涉順利，他怎麼回覆隨時告訴我。

reading.title: The Five Minutes Before the Meeting
paragraphs: Most meetings don't start on time. Someone is running behind, the projector won't connect, and five people sit around a table checking their phones. Although these few minutes feel wasted, they are often the most useful part of the meeting. This is when colleagues break the ice, swap news and find out what is really going on.

Good small talk is simple. Ask about something the other person has mentioned before: how a new teammate is settling in, how a hectic week is going, or whether a long commute has gotten any easier. People tend to remember who asked. However, there are limits. A colleague whose allergies have flared up might be happy to share the name of a good over-the-counter spray, whereas a long story about their symptoms is too much before a budget review.

Life outside work is fair game, too, as long as it stays light. Moving is a classic topic. Despite the stress of signing a new lease and waiting for the old landlord to return the security deposit, most people enjoy telling a funny story about it.

The best small talk also does a little work. A quick "Has anything carried over from last week?" can help a new hire get up to speed before the meeting even starts. And if someone mentions a problem, a simple "Keep me posted" shows that you were really listening. Whereas formal meetings make decisions, these five minutes build the trust that makes those decisions easier.

questions.q: According to the article, why are the minutes before a meeting useful?
options: Colleagues share news and learn what is really happening.
People can finish reading the agenda.
The manager explains the main decisions.
Everyone has time to answer emails.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段最後一句：This is when colleagues break the ice, swap news and find out what is really going on.

questions.q: Which topic does the writer say is too much before a budget review?
options: The name of a good over-the-counter spray
How a new teammate is settling in
A long story about someone's symptoms
A funny story about moving house
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：a long story about their symptoms is too much before a budget review。分享好用的成藥名稱反而可以。

questions.q: What can we infer about the phrase "Keep me posted" from the last paragraph?
options: It sounds too informal for most offices.
It is a small phrase that shows real attention.
Only managers should use it.
It is a polite way to end a conversation quickly.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：文章說 a simple "Keep me posted" shows that you were really listening，表示這句短短的話能讓對方感覺你有在聽、在關心。

grammar.point: Linking contrast: although, despite, whereas, however

guide.key_zh: although 接句子；despite 接名詞／V-ing；whereas 對比兩件事；However 開新句加逗號。

uses.label_zh: 儘管…（後面接名詞或動作）
兩個人或兩件事互相對比
uses.note_zh: 兩邊都是事實，只是不一樣
前一句用句號或分號結束，不能只用逗號

mistakes.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.right: Although it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.why_zh: despite 後面不能接完整句子（主詞＋動詞），要改用 although，或說 Despite the rain

mistakes.wrong: Although the apartment is small, but I like it.
mistakes.right: Although the apartment is small, I like it.
mistakes.why_zh: although 和 but 不能在同一句一起用

mistakes.wrong: I've emailed him twice, however he hasn't replied.
mistakes.right: I've emailed him twice. However, he hasn't replied.
mistakes.why_zh: however 不是連接詞，前面要用句號（或分號），後面加逗號

examples.en: Although the apartment is smaller, my commute is much shorter.
examples.zh: 雖然公寓比較小，但我的通勤時間短很多。

examples.en: Despite feeling awful, Priya finished the report on time.
examples.zh: 儘管身體很不舒服，Priya 還是準時完成報告。

examples.en: My old commute took an hour, whereas the new one takes fifteen minutes.
examples.zh: 我以前通勤要一小時，相對地，現在只要十五分鐘。

examples.en: I've emailed the landlord twice. However, he hasn't replied yet.
examples.zh: 我已經寫信給房東兩次了。不過他還沒回。

exercises.q: ___ the heavy traffic, Mark arrived only five minutes late. (despite / although)
exercises.explain_zh: 後面是名詞 the heavy traffic（沒有動詞），所以用 Despite。although 後面要接完整句子。

exercises.q: ___ my new apartment is smaller, I really like the neighborhood. (although / despite)
exercises.explain_zh: 後面是完整句子 my new apartment is smaller（主詞＋動詞），所以用 Although。

exercises.q: ___ working here for only two weeks, Ana already knows everyone. (despite / although)
exercises.explain_zh: 後面接的是 working（V-ing），不是完整句子，所以用 Despite；Although 後面要接「主詞＋動詞」：Although she has worked here…。

exercises.q: Despite ___ (feel) sick, Priya finished the report on time.
exercises.explain_zh: despite 後面接名詞或 V-ing，所以用 feeling，不是 feel 或 she felt。

exercises.q: Kevin likes working from the office, ___ Priya prefers working from home.
options: whereas
despite
however
in spite of
exercises.explain_zh: 兩個人的習慣互相對比、後面是完整句子，用 whereas。despite／in spite of 不接句子；however 不能用逗號接在句子中間。

exercises.q: I've asked the landlord for my deposit twice. ___, he still hasn't sent it.
options: Despite
Although
However
Whereas
exercises.explain_zh: 前一句已經用句號結束，新句子開頭表示轉折、後面有逗號，用 However。Despite、Although、Whereas 都要和另一個子句或名詞連在同一句。

listening.title: Waiting for Mark

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Morning, Priya. Looks like Mark's running behind again, so we've got a few minutes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Fine by me. How's the new place? Have you settled in yet?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Almost. Although the apartment is smaller, my commute is only fifteen minutes now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Nice. Did you get your security deposit back from your old landlord?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Not yet. I've emailed him twice, but he hasn't replied. It's been three weeks since I moved out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: That's annoying. My sister had the same problem when her last lease ended. Keep me posted.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Will do. How about you? You sounded terrible last week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: My allergies flared up, but I'm on the mend now. I've been taking an over-the-counter spray, and it's worked better than I expected.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Glad to hear it. And despite feeling awful, you still finished the report on time. Impressive.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: I did. However, a couple of tasks have carried over to this week, so I'll need to ask Mark for an extra day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Makes sense. Oh, and our new hire, Jun, starts on Monday. Could you help him get up to speed?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya

questions.q: Why do Kevin and Priya have time to chat?
options: The meeting room isn't ready.
Mark is late.
The meeting was moved to the afternoon.
Jun hasn't arrived yet.
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 第一句：Mark's running behind again, so we've got a few minutes. Mark 又晚到了。

questions.q: What is true about Kevin's new apartment?
options: It is bigger than his old one.
His commute is much shorter now.
He hasn't signed the lease yet.
His sister helped him find it.
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 說 Although the apartment is smaller, my commute is only fifteen minutes now. 公寓比較小，但通勤只要十五分鐘。

questions.q: Why will Priya probably ask Mark for an extra day?
options: She is still sick.
She has to train Jun all week.
Some of last week's work isn't finished.
She is moving house.
questions.explain_zh: Priya 說 a couple of tasks have carried over to this week，上週有幾項工作還沒做完，延到這週。她已經 on the mend，所以不是因為還在生病。

dictation: I've emailed him twice, but he hasn't replied.
I've been taking an over-the-counter spray, and it's worked better than I expected.
However, a couple of tasks have carried over to this week, so I'll need to ask Mark for an extra day.

shadowing: Looks like Mark's running behind again, so we've got a few minutes.
Although the apartment is smaller, my commute is only fifteen minutes now.
Despite feeling awful, you still finished the report on time.
I've emailed him twice, but he hasn't replied.

prompts.question: A colleague arrives early for a meeting. Start some small talk in one or two sentences, using although or despite.
prompts.question_zh: 同事提早到會議室。用一兩句話開始閒聊，句子裡用 although 或 despite。
prompts.sample: Morning! Despite the rain, you made it here early.

prompts.question: Tell a coworker about one recent change in your life and one thing you still haven't gotten around to.
prompts.question_zh: 跟同事說一件你最近生活中的改變，以及一件你還沒處理的事。
prompts.sample: I've recently moved closer to the office. However, I still haven't unpacked half of my boxes.

writing.task: Some of your work has carried over from last week because you were sick. Write a short email to your manager in three short paragraphs: (1) the problem, (2) what you've done so far, and (3) what you need next. Use at least two contrast words. Don't join two complete sentences with only a comma.
writing.task_zh: 你上週生病，有些工作延到這週。寫一封短信給主管，分三小段：(1) 問題是什麼；(2) 你目前做了什麼；(3) 接下來需要什麼。至少用兩個表示對比的字。不要只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起。
writing.sample:
Hi Mark,

Two tasks have carried over from last week. My allergies flared up on Tuesday, and I had to leave early twice. Although I worked late on Thursday, I couldn't finish the client report.

So far, I've completed the data section and checked the numbers with Priya. I've also started the summary. I'm on the mend now, so I'm back to my normal speed.

However, I still need one more day for the report. Could I send it to you on Wednesday instead of Tuesday? I'll keep you posted if anything changes.

Thanks,
Kevin
checklist_zh: 有沒有分成三小段：問題、目前做了什麼、接下來需要什麼
Although 後面接完整句子，而且同一句沒有再加 but
However 放在新句子開頭，前面是句號、後面有逗號
so far 後面用現在完成式（I've completed、I've started）
沒有只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起

reading.title: The Conversations That Don't Make the Minutes
paragraphs: When my company went hybrid, we were proud of how efficient our meetings became. Calls started on the dot, agendas were shared in advance, and nobody wasted ten minutes chatting about the weather. On paper, it was a triumph. In practice, something quietly went missing, and for months none of us could say what it was.

It took me a while to put my finger on it. Although we were hitting our deadlines, problems kept surfacing late. A designer would mention, almost in passing, that she'd been stuck for a week, whereas in the old office someone would have noticed her frustration by the coffee machine on day one. Small talk, it turns out, had been doing a job nobody had written down: it was our early-warning system.

Despite what the name suggests, small talk is rarely about small things. A question about someone's weekend can open the door to "Actually, I'm a bit swamped," and that admission is far easier to make over a casual chat than in front of a slide titled "Risks." It also lowers the stakes for newcomers, who are often reluctant to ask what an acronym means until they've built some rapport.

So we've started building the chat back in, deliberately. The first five minutes of our weekly call are now officially unstructured. However, we've learned that you can't simply order people to be spontaneous. What works is modeling it: the team lead goes first, admits something mildly embarrassing and asks a genuine follow-up question. It feels awkward for a couple of weeks, and some people will stay silent at first. Then, almost without anyone noticing, it stops feeling like part of the agenda and starts feeling like part of the team.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about the team's new, efficient meetings?
options: They hid problems that casual chat used to reveal early.
They made the team miss its deadlines.
They were especially popular with new hires.
They took longer than the old meetings.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第二段說 Although we were hitting our deadlines, problems kept surfacing late，以前在咖啡機旁就會發現的問題，現在拖很久才冒出來。截止日其實有趕上。

questions.q: According to the article, how does small talk help newcomers?
options: It helps them get promoted faster.
It means they don't have to present slides.
It makes basic questions easier to ask once they feel comfortable.
It replaces formal training.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：newcomers ... are often reluctant to ask what an acronym means until they've built some rapport。閒聊建立關係後，新人比較敢問基本問題。

questions.q: What does "you can't simply order people to be spontaneous" imply?
options: The unstructured time should be cancelled.
People dislike talking about their weekends.
Spontaneous meetings are always more efficient.
Casual chat has to be encouraged by example rather than demanded.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：下一句 What works is modeling it，由組長先示範分享、追問，才帶得起來；光是規定大家「要自然地聊」沒有用。

listening.title: First Week Nerves

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Tom, hi! Grab a seat. We're, uh, still waiting on half the team, so no rush.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Thanks. I wasn't sure if I was early or—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Or late? No, you're fine. Honestly, nobody here starts on the dot. So how's your first week treating you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Pretty well, actually. I'll admit, though, I'm drowning in acronyms. Everyone keeps saying QBR and I just nod.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Ha! Quarterly business review. Don't worry, it took me months to crack the code. You'll pick up the tech stuff in no time, whereas the jargon is a whole other story.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Good to know. And, um, is it normal that I still don't have access to the shared drive?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Ugh, no, that's on us. IT's been swamped since the office move. I'll chase it right after this meeting, I promise.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: I appreciate it. I just didn't want to seem—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Pushy? Not at all. Despite how it might feel, asking early is way better than sitting on a problem for a week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: That's a relief. At my last job, people kind of frowned on questions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Lena
lines.text: Well, here it's the opposite. Oh, here comes everyone. Shall we dive in?

questions.q: What is Tom finding hardest in his first week?
options: Finding the office
The company's acronyms and jargon
His manager's schedule
The project deadlines
questions.explain_zh: Tom 說 I'm drowning in acronyms，大家講 QBR 他只能點頭。

questions.q: Why does Lena say "that's on us"?
options: She accepts that the missing access is the company's fault.
She is blaming Tom for not asking sooner.
She thinks IT has already fixed the problem.
She wants Tom to contact IT himself.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：that's on us 是「是我們的責任」，接著她說 IT 很忙、她會親自去催，表示問題在公司這邊，不是 Tom。

questions.q: What can we infer about Tom's previous workplace?
options: It had better onboarding.
It used fewer acronyms.
Asking questions wasn't really welcome there.
Meetings always started late.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Tom 說 At my last job, people kind of frowned on questions，以前公司的人不太喜歡別人發問，所以他擔心顯得太 pushy。

dictation: IT's been swamped since the office move.
Despite how it might feel, asking early is way better than sitting on a problem for a week.

something that tells you about a problem before it becomes serious
having far too much work to deal with
a friendly relationship in which people understand each other
